lesson.scenario: A receiver uses per-sender sequence numbers and a holdback buffer when one sender’s messages arrive out of order.
entities: May delay, duplicate, or reorder packets
Indexes early packets by sequence number
Stores the next deliverable P sequence
Consumes P messages in send order

steps.title: Sender emits sequence 41
steps.narration: P assigns sequence 41 to debit before placing it on the channel.
steps.outcome: The packet carries enough metadata to recover P send order.
steps.invariant: One sender never reuses or decreases its sequence number within an epoch.

steps.title: Sender emits sequence 42
steps.narration: P sends receipt 42 after debit 41, but the channel gives it a shorter delay.
steps.outcome: Send order is 41 then 42 even though arrival order will differ.
steps.invariant: FIFO is scoped per sender; it does not compare unrelated senders.

steps.title: Early successor is held
steps.narration: Receipt 42 arrives first and cannot pass missing sequence 41.
steps.outcome: The application sees neither packet yet.
steps.invariant: A packet with sequence greater than nextExpected is buffered, never delivered early.

steps.title: Gap arrival drains contiguous order
steps.narration: Debit 41 arrives, is delivered, advances nextExpected to 42, and releases buffered receipt 42.
steps.invariant: Delivery advances only through a contiguous sequence prefix.

steps.title: Duplicate is discarded
steps.narration: A retransmitted receipt 42 arrives after nextExpected has advanced to 43.
steps.outcome: Retry traffic does not duplicate the application event.
steps.invariant: A sequence below nextExpected is stale or duplicate and cannot be redelivered under exactly-once FIFO delivery state.

production.scenario: A parcel-tracking platform uses FIFO delivery per package so customer status changes like loaded, departed, and delivered never apply out of order when scanners retry events.

flows: A dock scanner reports that parcel 981 has been loaded just before a van reconnects from a dead network spot.
The ingest API assigns the next package sequence and puts the event into the FIFO lane for parcel 981.
deliver next parcel event only after 441
The queue withholds sequence 442 until the earlier departed-the-sorting-center event is already acknowledged.
The projector updates the authoritative parcel record only after the queue releases the next contiguous event.
The shopper sees a clean status progression instead of delivered appearing before loaded-on-truck.
reinject failed parcel event into the same lane
If a consumer crashed mid-update, the replayer returns the event to the correct FIFO stream so later milestones still wait behind it.
